rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gospels omit Jesus’s speech after his birth and his arrival with his mother; Ibn ʿĀshūr finds the omission astonishing and evidence of imprecise Gospel transmission, while God disclosed it to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: كلام عيسى هذا مما أهملته أناجيل النصارى لأنهم طووا خبر وصولها إلى أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus begins by declaring servitude because God knew people would later claim that he was God’s son.
rows.anchor: والابتداء بوصف العبودية لله ألقاه الله على لسان عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense in “gave me the Book” expresses God’s prior decree that Jesus would receive it.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن إيتاء الكتاب بفعل المضي مراد به أن الله قدر إيتاءه إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Book can mean the Gospel, written revelation to Jesus, or the Torah, whose knowledge he received; on the Torah reading, being made a prophet marks a further rank.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكتاب الإنجيل وهو ما كتب من الوحي الذي خاطب الله به عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessed means accompanied by good and blessing in conduct and speech; Jesus’s greatest blessing was mercy to Israel, easing some prohibitions and renewing virtue, while his presence brought guidance and reform.
rows.anchor: الذي تقارن البركة أحواله في أعماله ومحاورته ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus transformed ordinary, often unlettered disciples such as fishermen and tax collectors into wise guides whose hearts opened to faith.
rows.anchor: ولذلك ترى أكثر الحواريين كانوا من عامة الأميين من صيادين وعشارين فصاروا دعاة هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being blessed is broader than being a prophet, so the two descriptions are not redundant.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يظهر أن كونه مباركا أعم من كونه نبيئا عموما وجهيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Wherever I am” generalizes across places: Jesus’s blessing accompanied him beyond the Temple or his own town.
rows.anchor: بل هو حيثما حل تحل معه البركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense of “enjoined me” expresses God’s decree; وصاية is a firmly emphasized command for future action.
rows.anchor: أي أن يأمرني بهما أمرا مؤكدا مستمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat here is almsgiving, a personal command for Jesus like the Prophet’s night prayer; “as long as I live” means frequent practice when circumstances permit, not uninterrupted performance.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر خاص به كما أمر نبيئنا صلى الله عليه وسلم بقيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are not prescribed rites for Jesus’s community: the context lists his distinctive traits, and he brought no prayer law beyond the Torah.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يأت بشرع صلاة زائدة على ما شرع في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’s exceptional dutifulness to his mother answered weak filial piety among Israelites, especially toward mothers who were vulnerable to neglect.
rows.anchor: لأن بر الوالدين كان ضعيفا في بني إسرائيل يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabbār means arrogant and harsh in dealings; shaqī means a loser with painful circumstances, opposite saʿīd, and describing a tyrant as wretched points to his outcome, perhaps in this life too.
rows.anchor: الخاسر والذي تكون أحواله كدرة له ومؤلمة ، وهو ضد السعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clarification identifies the real Jesus against Jews who debase him and Christians who deify him; it distinguishes his true attributes, not his person from another person.
rows.anchor: والإشارة لتمييز المذكور أكمل تمييز تعريضا بالرد على اليهود والنصارى جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers raise qawl al-ḥaqq as a second predicate, a description of Jesus, or an apposition; Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb read it in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: بالرفع ، وقرأه ابن عامر ، وعاصم ، ويعقوب بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawl al-ḥaqq may mean that the stated attributes are the true account, or that Jesus himself is God’s true utterance, created by “Be”; qawl then means what is spoken, like khalq in 31:11.
rows.anchor: أن تلك الصفات التي سمعتم هي قول الحق

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī allows the accusative as an emphatic verbal noun from an implicit “I affirm the truth,” or as a verbal noun replacing “I say the truth.”
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو علي الفارسي أن يكون نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis makes qawl a verbal noun meaning speaker, describing Jesus as truthful in the speech from “I am God’s servant” through his resurrection statement.
rows.anchor: مصدرا نائبا عن فعله ، أي أقول قول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration may continue Jesus’s speech affirming his mother’s innocence, with the preceding material as an interruption; it teaches that God is Lord of all creatures.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا بقية لكلام جرى على لسان عيسى تأييدا لبراءة أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the opening hamza, read by Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Ruways from Yaʿqūb, al-Zamakhsharī supplies a causal lām; if Jesus speaks, God’s lordship grounds the command to worship him.
rows.anchor: فخرجه الزمخشري أنه على تقدير لام التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the same reading, the clause may instead coordinate with the command to pray and give zakat, with a preposition omitted before أن.
rows.anchor: أي وأوصاني بأن الله ربي وربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause may coordinate with “word of truth,” if qawl means speaker, making Jesus both speaker of truth and speaker that God is his and their Lord.
rows.anchor: أي قائل الحق وقائل إن الله ربي وربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If addressed to the Prophet, an implicit “say” may introduce it, or it may coordinate with “remember Mary”; worship then follows from the denial that God has a child.
rows.anchor: وإن كان مما خوطب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن يقوله كان بتقدير قول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Rawḥ from Yaʿqūb read the hamza with kasra, fitting either broad syntactic interpretation.
rows.anchor: ووجهها ظاهر على كلا الاحتمالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This is a straight path” sums up what precedes, whatever syntactic analysis is adopted.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى مضمون ما تقدم على اختلاف الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path signifies true belief, metaphorically likened to a direct road that safely delivers its traveler to guidance; other paths lead to danger.
rows.anchor: في كونه موصولا إلى الهدى بالصراط المستقيم في إيصاله إلى المكان المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء links the factions’ disagreement to their departure from the straight path: those following it do not fundamentally disagree, while divergent paths split the factions.
rows.anchor: الفاء لتفريع الإخبار بحصول الاختلاف على الإخبار بأن هذا صراط مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in “among themselves” reinforces the meaning: they disagreed with one another.
rows.anchor: حرف توكيد ، أي اختلفوا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The factions are Christians: they had shared monotheism in the apostles’ lifetime, then divided among their disciples; Jews had never shared their religion.
rows.anchor: لأن الاختلاف مؤذن بأنهم كانوا متفقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christian divisions include Melkites, Jacobites, and Nestorians and later branches; the Arab Rukūsiyya mixed Christianity with Ṣābian beliefs, as mentioned in a report to ʿAdī b. Ḥātim, and Protestants followed Luther.
rows.anchor: ورد ذكرها في الحديث : أن النبي قال لعدي بن حاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dispute centers on Jesus’s divinity, based on misunderstanding “son,” although the Gospels call his followers sons and describe Jesus as son of man with God as his Lord; the warning includes Christians and other polytheists.
rows.anchor: ولما كان اختلافهم قد انحصر في مرجع واحد يرجع إلى إلهية عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forms of amazement may voice the Prophet and believers or be used to cause wonder; they also threaten by marveling at the disbelievers’ capacity to hear and see what they hate.
rows.anchor: وهو تعجب على لسان الرسول والمؤمنين ، أو هو مستعمل في التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the forms as ordinary imperatives to an unspecified hearer: hear and see through them, with the objects generalized and omitted; this too threatens.
rows.anchor: غير مستعمل في التعجب بل صادف أن جاء على صورة فعل التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to those who disbelieved, including Christians and idol worshippers.
rows.anchor: أي أعجب بحالهم يومئذ من نصارى وعبدة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast says wrongdoers are already in manifest worldly misguidance, correcting any impression that their present condition is comfortable before their future misery.
rows.anchor: من ترقب سوء حالهم يوم القيامة الذي يقتضي الظن بأنهم الآن في سعة من الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them wrongdoers instead of repeating the pronoun transitions to idolaters, whom Qur’anic usage calls wrongdoers because associating partners is grave injustice.
rows.anchor: ونكتته التخلص إلى خصوص المشركين لأن اصطلاح القرآن إطلاق الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning of the afterlife and naming their worldly error, the discourse commands warning them to complete the presentation of the case.
rows.anchor: عقب تحذيرهم من عذاب الآخرة والنداء على سوء ضلالهم في الدنيا بالأمر بإنذارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warned wrongdoers are idolaters among Meccans and elsewhere, identified by the clauses about unbelief and return to God.
rows.anchor: وهم المشركون من أهل مكة وغيرهم من عبدة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Day of regret” is the second object of “warn,” meaning punishment on Judgment Day, when wrongdoers intensely regret lost chances; it is their day of regret, though a day of joy for the righteous.
rows.anchor: والمراد بيوم الحسرة يوم الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The article in “the regret” may mark a mentally familiar event or replace a possessive phrase, meaning the wrongdoers’ regret.
rows.anchor: واللام في الحسرة على هذا الوجه لام العهد الذهني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The matter was decided” may mean God’s decree to drive them into punishment was completed and cannot be reversed, or that the decree for Resurrection arrived.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قضى الأمر : تمم أمر الله بزجهم في العذاب فلا معقب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Resurrection reading, إذ substitutes for “Day of regret”; the heedlessness clause is circumstantial and warns that the Day may arrive suddenly, as in 7:187, which Ibn ʿĀshūr finds more fitting here.
rows.anchor: على الاحتمال الثاني تحذير من حلول يوم القيامة بهم قبل أن يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect “they do not believe” depicts unbelief continuing persistently until the decree arrives, emphasizing its extraordinary duration.
rows.anchor: ومعنى وهم لا يؤمنون استمرار عدم إيمانهم إلى حلول قضاء الأمر يوم الحسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a concluding coda at the end of the story, directed to the polytheists.
rows.anchor: تذييل لختم القصة على عادة القرآن في تذييل الأغراض عند الانتقال منها إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns return to everyone on earth and to those whom the Prophet was told to warn.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى من عليها وإلى ما عاد إليه ضمير الغيبة في وأنذرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance is a metaphor for God’s becoming the sole possessor of control after creatures perish; their delegated participation ends, and His control includes requital.
rows.anchor: فإذا هلك الناس والحيوان فقد صاروا في باطن الأرض وصارت الأرض في غير تصرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic opening counters polytheists who deny recompense and therefore deny God’s inheritance of earth in this sense.
rows.anchor: بحرف التوكيد لدفع الشك لأن المشركين ينكرون الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separate pronoun نحن only emphasizes the claim; Ibn ʿĀshūr says it does not imply exclusivity because no contrary belief is being rebutted.
rows.anchor: وأما ضمير الفصل في قوله نحن نرث الأرض فهو لمجرد التأكيد ولا يفيد تخصيصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He observes that this emphatic pronoun often follows another pronoun, as in “I am God” and “they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.”
rows.anchor: نحو قوله إنني أنا الله في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coda threatens that polytheists will be in the one Lord’s grasp, their idols cannot benefit them, and God will inherit even those idols.
rows.anchor: وأفاد هذا التذييل التعريف بتهديد المشركين بأنهم لا مفر لهم من الكون في قبضة الرب الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “to Us” conveys that none return elsewhere; for Muslims the emphasis expresses concern, while for polytheists it asserts exclusivity.
rows.anchor: فالتقديم مفيد القصر ، أي لا يرجعون إلى غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham belongs among the surah’s purposes as father of prophets and the first to establish enduring public monotheism through the Kaaba; Arabs inherited him but practiced polytheism.
rows.anchor: أبا الأنبياء وأول من أعلن التوحيد إعلانا باقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing Abraham after Jesus and before the other prophets is rhetorically apt and consoles the Prophet through the parallel between Abraham’s people and his own persecutors.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك تسلية للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم على ما لقي من مشركي قومه لمشابهة حالهم بحال قوم إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abraham narrative is told in a manner resembling Mary’s story because both are important.
rows.anchor: وقد جرى سرد خبر إبراهيم عليه السلام على أسلوب سرد قصة مريم عليها السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq is an intensive form, illustrated by titles and words such as al-Malik al-Ḍalīl, misk, ḥarīf, and kharrīt; Abraham merits it for extreme truthfulness in obeying God, even attempting his son’s sacrifice.
rows.anchor: مثل الملك الضليل لقب امرىء القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic innahu kāna construction reinforces praise by stressing the truth of Abraham’s description.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد هذا الخبر بحرف التوكيد وبإقحام فعل الكون للاهتمام بتحقيقه زيادة في الثناء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He was truthful, a prophet” explains why Abraham merits mention and interrupts the mention-to-substitute construction; his address to his father exemplifies truthfulness.
rows.anchor: واقعة موقع التعليل للاهتمام بذكره في التلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophet is a passive form meaning one informed by God’s revelation; commonly it denotes a messenger in customary religious usage, while a prophet need not be commissioned to convey revelation.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا أنه منبأ من جانب الله تعالى بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s rebuke to his father came by revelation so he could convey the invalidity of idol worship to his people.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن قوله لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر إنما كان عن وحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce nabiyyan with doubled y after easing the hamza; Nāfiʿ alone reads nabīʾan with hamza, producing an alif rhyme like many Qur’anic endings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور نبيا بياء مشددة بتخفيف الهمزة ياء لثقلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal clause “when he said to his father” is an appositive specifying Abraham, and its time is singled out as especially worthy of remembrance.
rows.anchor: اذكر إبراهيم زمان قوله لأبيه فإن ذلك الوقت أجدر أوقات إبراهيم بأن يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s father was Āzar, previously identified in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: تقدم ذكره في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added vocative summons the father’s attention despite his physical presence; Abraham begins with sensory evidence, then addresses resistance to taking advice from a son.
rows.anchor: وافتتح إبراهيم خطابه أباه بندائه مع أن الحضرة مغنية عن النداء قصدا لإحضار سمعه وذهنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr’s grandfather explains that the question leads the father to see he cannot justify worshipping what cannot hear or see; the uselessness argument follows, then Abraham anticipates the father’s resistance to a younger adviser.
rows.anchor: علم إبراهيم أن في طبع أهل الجهالة تحقيرهم للصغير كيفما بلغ حاله في الحذق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grandfather’s account traces the appeal from sensory evidence and uselessness to the son’s limited knowledge, then Satan’s influence, and finally a hypothetical warning that idols cannot punish desertion.
rows.anchor: فلما قضى حق ذلك انتقل إلى تنبيهه على أن ما هو فيه أثر من وساوس الشيطان

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A couplet attributed to ʿAlī says that if astrologer and physician are right about no resurrection, the speaker loses nothing; if he is right, their loss is theirs.
rows.anchor: زعم المنجم والطبيب كلاهمالا تحشر الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham repeats “O father” four times to persuade gently; this expansive setting contrasts with Noah’s single address to his son in a concise setting.
rows.anchor: أربع مرات تكرير اقتضاه مقام استنزاله إلى قبول الموعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers the literal question analysis, following al-Kashshāf: the question indirectly denies any valid reason for idol worship and challenges the father to supply one.
rows.anchor: الوجه ما بني عليه من أن الاستفهام مستعمل في حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rhetorical double entendre that conveys the father’s inability to provide the requested reason for worship.
rows.anchor: فهو كناية عن التعجيز عن إبداء المسؤول عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā abati derives from abī: the speaker’s yā is replaced irregularly by tāʾ in vocative use with father or mother, perhaps preserving an old Arabic form.
rows.anchor: حذفوا ياء المتكلم وعوضوا عنها تاء تعويضا على غير قياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayhi says the tāʾ becomes hāʾ in pause; al-Farrāʾ says it remains tāʾ.
rows.anchor: أن التاء تصير في الوقف هاء ، وخالفه الفراء فقال : ببقائها في الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use kasra on tāʾ; Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar read it with fatḥa and no following alif, as if an alif after open vocative yāʾ were dropped.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر : ( يأبت ) بفتح التاء دون ألف بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the fatherly vocative renews attention and expresses sincere counsel; al-Kashshāf says Abraham invites him gently without calling him ignorant or claiming overwhelming knowledge.
rows.anchor: إعادة ندائه بوصف الأبوة تأكيد لإحضار الذهن ولإمحاض النصيحة

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf’s analogy says that if a traveler knows the route while his companion does not, following him prevents straying; Abraham means revealed knowledge and prophecy.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن أباه كان يرى نفسه على علم عظيم لأنه كان كبير ديانة قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining that idol worship obeys Satan and disobeys God, Abraham warns that his father may lose divine mercy, suffer punishment, and share Satan’s fate as an ally.
rows.anchor: لا جرم أنه لما قرر له أن عبادته الأصنام اتباع لأمر الشيطان عصي الرحمن انتقل إلى توقع حرمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God al-Raḥmān highlights that punishment means deprivation from the mercy characteristic of the one who punishes.
rows.anchor: وللإشارة إلى أن أصل حلول العذاب بمن يحل به هو الحرمان من الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walī means companion or follower sharing another’s condition; it euphemistically signals their common final destiny.
rows.anchor: فكني بالولاية عن المقارنة في المصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says “I fear” rather than asserting certainty, showing deference concerning God’s acts and preserving hope that his father can escape punishment by abandoning idols.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالخوف الدال على الظن دون القطع تأدب مع الله تعالى بأن لا يثبت أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Becoming Satan’s ally means following Satan into punishment.
rows.anchor: فتكون في اتباع الشيطان في العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “he said” explicitly separates the dialogue, as in another Qur’anic dialogue.
rows.anchor: لوقوعها في المحاورة كما تقدم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father’s question indignantly rejects Abraham’s departure from idol worship; possessively attaching the idols to himself asserts his authority and honors himself.
rows.anchor: إضافة الآلهة إلى ضمير نفسه إضافة ولاية وانتساب إلى المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father answers with rudeness and arrogance, unlike Abraham’s gentleness, revealing hardness of heart and entrenched disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في جوابه دعوة ابنه بمنتهى الجفاء والعنجهية بعكس ما في كلام إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to leave coordinates with the threat: stoning is a deferred penalty, while exclusion from company and conversation is immediate.
rows.anchor: وجملة واهجرني مليا عطف على جملة لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hajr means cutting conversation and companionship; ordering his son to leave rather than announcing his own departure casts it as expulsion and humiliation.
rows.anchor: قطع المكالمة وقطع المعاشرة ، وإنما أمر أبو إبراهيم ابنه بهجرانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maliyyan means a long time, with no known simple verb or verbal noun; it derives from a disused source and modifies an omitted cognate object, “a long abandonment.”
rows.anchor: ومليا : طويلا ، وهو فعيل ، ولا يعرف له فعل مجرد ولا مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, maliyyan modifies an omitted time noun, since al-malā often means a period; the explanation compares this ellipsis with the expression “a ship with planks.”
rows.anchor: بناء على أن الملا مقصورا غالب في الزمان فذكره يغني عن ذكر موصوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s “peace be upon you” is a farewell of separation, offered before anything else to show he does not resent leaving for God’s sake.
rows.anchor: وبادره به قبل الكلام الذي أعقبه به إشارة إلى أنه لا يسوءه ذلك الهجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s forbearance answers his father’s harshness with kindness at their final moment.
rows.anchor: مثوبة بالإحسان في معاملته في آخر لحظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām means safety, and ʿalā expresses figurative establishment; the greeting is an expression of honor.
rows.anchor: و ( على ) للاستعلاء المجازي وهو التمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham hopes for his father’s guidance and asks forgiveness for past shirk by asking God to guide him to monotheism; no prohibition had yet been revealed, as shown in 9:114 and 26:86.
rows.anchor: بأن يهديه الله إلى التوحيد فيغفر له الشرك الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text omits the completed separation after stating Abraham’s resolve, then names God’s reward: descendants who would comfort him in his loneliness, Isaac and Jacob, both prophets.
rows.anchor: طوي ذكر اعتزاله إياهم بعد أن ذكر عزمه عليه إيجازا في الكلام للعلم بأن مثله لا يعزم أمرا إلا نفذ عزمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward was not limited to Isaac and Jacob; Abraham also received Ishmael, and all three gifts followed his departure from his people.
rows.anchor: وليس مجازاة الله إبراهيم مقصورة على أن وهبه إسحاق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isaac and Jacob are named because Sarah also left her people, so the two were a shared gift and close companions matching Abraham’s sacrifice.
rows.anchor: أن وهب لهما إسحاق وبعده يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael lived far away in Mecca to neighbor the House of God, a greater proximity than living with his father and brother.
rows.anchor: أما إسماعيل فقد أراد الله أن يكون بعيدا عن إبراهيم في مكة ليكون جار بيت الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael receives separate mention in 38:48; Ibn ʿĀshūr also identifies the gentle boy promised after Abraham’s migration in 37:99–101 as Ishmael.
rows.anchor: وقد خص إسماعيل بالذكر استقلالا عقب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses follows Abraham and Jacob because he was the most distinguished prophet descended from Isaac and Jacob.
rows.anchor: أفضت مناسبة ذكر إبراهيم ويعقوب إلى أن يذكر موسى في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about remembering Moses and describing him is independent prose rather than the parenthetical construction used for Abraham.
rows.anchor: كالقول في نظيريهما في ذكر إبراهيم عدا أن الجملة هنا غير معترضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use kasra in mukhliṣan, meaning sincere; Ḥamza, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf use fatḥa in mukhlaṣan, meaning chosen by God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور مخلصا بكسر اللام من أخلص القاصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s sincerity was shown when he confronted Pharaoh fearlessly and refused to aid criminals; his being chosen is shown by God speaking directly to him before an angel conveyed revelation.
rows.anchor: فإنه أخلص في الدعوة إلى الله فاستخف بأعظم جبار وهو فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger is necessarily a prophet sent to convey revelation, while a prophet may receive revelation without being commissioned to convey it; calling Moses a prophet after messenger reinforces his strong mission.
rows.anchor: فلأن الرسول هو المرسل بوحي من الله ليبلغ إلى الناس فلا يكون الرسول إلا نبيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael merits separate mention after Abraham and Isaac because he founded an independent nation earlier, was Abraham’s firstborn, and helped build the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: خص إسماعيل بالذكر هنا تنبيها على جدارته بالاستقلال بالذكر عقب ذكر إبراهيم وابنه إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is famed for keeping promises, a virtue inherited by his descendants; his greatest fulfilled promise was to endure sacrifice, as he told Abraham.
rows.anchor: وخصه بوصف صدق الوعد لأنه اشتهر به وتركه خلقا في ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was sent to his people, initially his mother, children, and Jurhum in-laws; later Arabs descended from him and were also his family, following Abraham’s prayer, almsgiving, and hanif religion.
rows.anchor: وهم يومئذ لا يعدون أهله أمه وبنيه وأصهاره من جرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being pleased with Ishmael means granting him abundant favor: blessing and multiplying his descendants, making the noblest prophet his descendant, and sending the great law through a descendant.
rows.anchor: إذ باركه وأنمى نسله وجعل أشرف الأنبياء من ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of nabiyyan with hamza or doubled y, and the distinction between messenger and prophet, were discussed above in the treatments of Jesus and Moses.
rows.anchor: وتقدم اختلاف القراء في قراءة نبيئا بالهمز أو بالياء المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the prophets and servants named from the opening mention of Zakariyyā onward; it signals they deserve the ensuing praise because of their qualities.
rows.anchor: من قوله { ذكر رحمة ربك عبده زكرياء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s blessings, guidance, and choosing reward their deeds and prophetic or truthful distinction; attributing these gifts to God further honors them.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك أحسن جزاء على ما قدموه من الأعمال ، ومن أعطوه من مزايا النبوءة والصديقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce al-nabiyyīn with two yāʾs after bāʾ; Nāfiʿ alone reads it with hamza after bāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأه نافع وحده بهمزة بعد الموحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about recitation is independent and describes gratitude and closeness to God expressed through prostration and weeping.
rows.anchor: مستأنفة دالة على شكرهم نعم الله عليهم وتقريبه إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their weeping arises from a mixed emotional response of reverence and fear.
rows.anchor: والمراد به البكاء الناشىء عن انفعال النفس انفعالا مختلطا من التعظيم والخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujjadan is the plural of sājid, while bukiyyan is a heard plural of bākin, derived through assimilation of wāw into yāʾ.
rows.anchor: والثاني وزنه فعول جمع فاعل مثل قوم قعود

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s narrated practice makes this verse a Qur’anic prostration site; believers prostrate in imitation of the prophets praised for prostrating at revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية من مواضع سجود القرآن المروية عن النبي اقتداء بأولئك الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from praise to condemn later descendants who failed to follow righteous forebears; khalaf with a still l means bad successors, unlike khalaf with a fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فرع على الثناء عليهم اعتبار وتنديد بطائفة من ذرياتهم لم يقتدوا بصالح أسلافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These successors include all errant nations descended from Noah or Abraham, including Arabs through Ishmael and Israelites through Jacob.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا يشمل جميع الأمم التي ضلت لأنها راجعة في النسب إلى إدريس جد نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “After them” spans many generations; it is not a necessary restriction, but evokes the passing of the righteous.
rows.anchor: يشمل طبقات وقرونا كثيرة ، ليس قيدا لأن الخلف لا يكون إلا من بعد أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasting prayer is a metaphor for neglecting precious worship; they followed desires that inclined toward corruption.
rows.anchor: مجاز في التفريط بتشبيهه بإهمال العرض النفيس ، فرطوا في عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer here means worshipping God alone.
rows.anchor: والصلاة : عبادة الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasting prayer and following desire encompass disbelief and immorality: shirk abandons worship and follows desire without proof, while Jews and Christians neglected prayers and invented desires.
rows.anchor: وهذان وصفان جامعان لأصناف الكفر والفسوق ، فالشرك إضاعة للصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayy means error and can mean evil; it may mean the punishment for error, as in the punishment for sins, a reading supported by the contrast with entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: والغي : الضلال ، ويطلق على الشر ، كما أطلق ضده وهو الرشد على الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawfa makes their meeting with ghayy a repeated future event, intensifying the warning against persisting in these sins.
rows.anchor: وحرف ( سوف ) دال على أن لقاءهم الغي متكرر في أزمنة المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative honors repentant believers and encourages conversion; the present-tense “enter” indicates no delay in their reward.
rows.anchor: جيء في جانبهم باسم الإشارة إشادة بهم وتنبيها لهم للترغيب في توبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Janna is the proper name of the reward’s abode, containing many gardens as an unnamed hadith states.
rows.anchor: علم لدار الثواب والنعيم . وفيها جنات كثيرة كما ورد في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulm here means shortchanging, injustice, or delay; shayʾ means an existent thing, not the verbal noun of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: هنا بمعنى النقص والإجحاف والمطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite shayʾan under negation denies every instance of shortchanging or delay, reassuring converts that prior disbelief will not diminish their final reward.
rows.anchor: وذكر شيئا في سياق النفي يفيد نفي كل فرد من أفراد النقص والإجحاف والإبطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural gardens appositively explains the singular Paradise, which contains many gardens; ʿAdn means abiding residence.
rows.anchor: جيء بصيغة جمع جنات مع أن المبدل منه مفرد لأنه يشتمل على جنات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the gardens as promised by the Merciful honors them and folds encouragement of present disbelievers into the promise to earlier believers.
rows.anchor: لزيادة تشريفها وتحسينها . وفي ذلك إدماج لتبشير المؤمنين السابقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayb is what is hidden from sight; the preposition means the promise was made in an unseen time, before the gardens were visible to their recipients, while already prepared for them.
rows.anchor: فكل ما غاب عن المشاهدة فهو غيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God’s promise is coming explains and confirms the promise of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعدا من الله واقعا . وهذا تحقيق للبشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of salām is disconnected: an apparent exception asserts something resembling the opposite, as in al-Nābigha’s line about swords with chips; it means they hear greetings.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع وهو مجاز من تأكيد الشيء بما يشبه ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq means food.
rows.anchor: والرزق : الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence signals stable, continuing provision more strongly than a verb; fronting the phrase and attaching the possessive pronoun emphasize their special share.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالجملة الاسمية للدلالة على ثبات ذلك ودوامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning is the first half of the day and evening the second; naming both implies provision throughout time, whenever desired, so night need not be named.
rows.anchor: والبكرة : النصف الأول من النهار ، والعشي : النصف الأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new sentence and demonstrative single out Paradise; its relative description honors the pious as its rightful recipients, like the gardens prepared for the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: مستأنفة ابتدائية . واسم الإشارة لزيادة التمييز تنويها بشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuwarith means make someone inherit or give an inheritance; here inheritance is a metaphor for a gift stored for its recipient, not literal succession after a relative’s death.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الإرث : انتقال مال القريب إلى قريبه بعد موته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use a still wāw and light rāʾ in nuwrith; Ruways from Yaʿqūb reads a fatḥa and doubled rāʾ from the intensive verb.
rows.anchor: بسكون الواو بعد الضمة وتخفيف الراء ، وقرأه رويس عن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the verse’s placement unusual but accepts the report from Ibn ʿAbbās as its most reliable and fitting occasion of revelation: Gabriel delayed, and the Prophet asked him to visit more often.
rows.anchor: فقال جمهور المفسرين : إن سبب نزولها أن جبريل عليه السلام أبطأ أياما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report transmitted by al-Bukhārī and al-Tirmidhī says the Prophet asked Gabriel to visit more often after Gabriel’s delayed visits.
rows.anchor: رواه البخاري والترمذي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands Gabriel to say the verse as an answer to the Prophet; an implicit “say” is omitted, and the verse was fixed where revelation had reached after the preceding prophetic stories.
rows.anchor: أن الله أمر جبريل عليه السلام أن يقول هذا الكلام جوابا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s question came at the end of the prophetic stories; the verse entered the Qur’an at the point revelation had reached.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ذلك لجبريل عليه السلام عند انتهاء قصص الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Gabriel and the angels: they descend and meet messengers only at God’s command, never by their own choice.
rows.anchor: أعلم الله نبيئه على لسان جبريل أن نزول الملائكة لا يقع إلا عن أمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanazzul means descend; its form suggests exertion because angels’ descent from their realm is unusual, as also in the Night of Decree verse.
rows.anchor: مرادف ننزل ، وأصل التنزل : تكلف النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in lahu marks ownership of governance; before, behind, and between cover the front, back, right, and left, encompassing directions.
rows.anchor: واللام في ( له ) للملك ، وهو ملك التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the spatial regions belong to God, they stand metonymically for their contents; the expression encompasses all beings, their states and actions, and past, present, and future times.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ذلك مخبرا عنه بأنه ملك لله تعين أن يراد به الكائنات التي في تلك الجهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse answers the Prophet through Gabriel, “not forgetful” can mean God does not abandon him; the intensified form can emphasize the long interval before resuming revelation.
rows.anchor: بتارك ، أي ما كان ربك تاركك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nasiya is an intensive negation of forgetfulness, affirming God’s comprehensive knowledge: angels descend only when His knowledge and wisdom call for it.
rows.anchor: فيتعين صرف المبالغة إلى جانب نسبة نفي النسيان عن الله

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم وصاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Abū Muslim and al-Kashshāf allow the verse to continue the speech of Paradise’s inhabitants: they descend there only by their Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية من تمام حكاية كلام أهل الجنة بتقدير فعل يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that alternative, the address “your Lord” is one speaker addressing another; “your Lord was not forgetful” may be God’s coda to the Prophet or the people of Paradise affirming their Lord kept His promise.
rows.anchor: من قول الله تعالى لرسوله تذييلا لما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse begins a new divine address to the Prophet, concluding that angels act only by their Lord’s leave and all creation is under God’s control, then commanding worship.
rows.anchor: من كلام الله تعالى كما يقتضيه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord of the heavens” is the predicate of an omitted subject; usage requires omitting it when a final distinguishing description follows other descriptions.
rows.anchor: على الخبرية لمبتدأ محذوف ملتزم الحذف في المقام الذي يذكر فيه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verse attributed uncertainly to al-Ṣūlī or Ibn al-Zubayr illustrates the omitted subject before a final predicate.
rows.anchor: كقول الصولي أو ابن الزبير بفتح الزاي وكسر الموحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are upper worlds, earth the lower world, and what lies between them the skies and horizons; together the three cover all beings.
rows.anchor: العوالم العلوية . والأرض : العالم السفلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worship and patience commands address the Prophet, derive naturally from God’s universal control, and transition to affirming monotheism while condemning association.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في { فاعبده واصطبر } و { هل تعلم } للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣṭibār is intense patience; although normally followed by ʿalā, the lām here conveys steadfastness because worship includes varied struggles of self-mastery.
rows.anchor: والاصطبار : شدة الصبر على الأمر الشاق ، لأن صيغة الافتعال ترد لإفادة قوة الفعل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says the ʿishāʾ prayer is the heaviest prayer for hypocrites, illustrating why worship requires firmness.
rows.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة العشاء : ( هي أثقل صلاة على المنافقين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question about whether anyone is God’s samiyy explains why He alone deserves worship and why the Prophet should persevere.
rows.anchor: وجملة { هل تعلم له سميا } واقعة موقع التعليل للأمر بعبادته والاصطبار عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets samiyy as a counterpart or equal, derived from musāmāh; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers this sense, which means comparable in all attributes.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس أنه فسره بالنظير ، مأخوذا من المساماة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred sense, the interrogative is a denial: no being exists who equals or resembles God.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إنكاري ، أي لا مسامي لله تعالى ، أي ليس من يساميه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes samiyy as someone with the same name, like the description of John in 19:7; no idol is called “Allah,” and their failure to claim creative power acknowledges God’s uniqueness.
rows.anchor: المماثل في الاسم . كقوله في ذكر يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternate reading also grounds exclusive worship: people do not know a namesake, and the absence of a known equal entails that no other being deserves worship.
rows.anchor: وكني بانتفاء العلم بسميه عن انتفاء وجود سمي له ، لأن العلم يستلزم وجود المعلوم
